> 4. Bench: tests/stub-launch.toml, arch rv64 and rv32, debug_assertions on. The launch path works with existing calls (process_create, process_map, process_start), so there was nothing to escalate. The parent is tests/programs/src/bin/stub-launch.rs. Children run in their own budget under USERS. After every child, the parent requires that budget's usage to equal empty exactly.
> The cases and their results:
> - well-formed child: exits 77
> - 111 each: overlapping segments; segment over the stub; segment over the startup page; segment over the stack; entry in a read-only segment; entry outside every segment; truncated file header; truncated program headers
> - huge image_len: exits 110
> - segment bytes past the mapped image: faults (13)
> - 32 header-fuzzed images, fixed xorshift seed: each ends with an exit or fault notice (all 32 exited)
> - a final well-formed child: exits 77
> 
> Two layouts: the stack and startup page sit either outside the link range (0x8000_0000 / 0x7FF0_0000) or inside it (0x1000_0000 / 0x0F00_0000). The "segment over the stack" case passes the stub's plan, so it exercises the kernel's map_fixed InvalidArgument path. Mutation check: mapping `Either::B(_)` to MAP_UNAVAILABLE makes that case FAIL (exited 112).
> 
> Found and fixed along the way, in tests/programs/build.rs:
> - (a) The script only watched its own output, so an edited stub could stay stale in the bench. My first mutation run falsely PASSED because of this. It now watches stub/src, link.x, build.rs, Cargo.toml, libs/sys/src and libs/wire/src (build.rs:57-60).
> - (b) fixture-child is now `rust-objcopy --strip-all`ed (build.rs:46-53). The rv32 build carried 18 KB of debug sections, which overflowed the launcher's 4 KiB copy buffer and killed the parent silently.
> 
> launch() now returns the failing step (a FAIL line) instead of panicking with no output. It doesn't close the process handle: receiving the exit notice frees it (KERNEL-SPEC, Process), and closing it gave BadHandle.
